\section[dāhaṁ]{\ml{ദാഹം} (dāhaṁ) — thirst}

\label{lesson:ML-C117-thirst}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for laughter, then the Malayalam for worry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ദാഹം}}
\textbf{\ml{ദാഹം}} (\emph{dāhaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}thirst\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ദാഹമുണ്ട്}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am thirsty\textquotedblright{}, built like \textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{വിശപ്പുണ്ട്}}, \textquotedblleft{}I am hungry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Hunger's partner.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāhaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāhaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{enikkŭ dāhamuṇṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for laughter, then the Malayalam for worry, then say \emph{dāhaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ദാഹം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thirst\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
